2027-04-06.title: Tuesday of the Second Week of Easter
readings: The community of believers was of one heart and soul
The Lord is king; he is robed in majesty (or: Alleluia)
No one has gone up to heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man
2027-04-06.alt: Easter weekday of the Second Week of Easter. The Alleluia is sung before the Gospel; the Regina Caeli replaces the Angelus until Pentecost. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-06.verse: And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
theo: St Luke paints a second portrait of the first community in Jerusalem: “the whole group of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one claimed private ownership of any possessions, but everything they owned was held in common.” This is not a political programme; it is what the Resurrection does to people. In the middle of the passage Luke places its source: “With great power the apostles gave their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.” Because Christ is risen, nobody needs to cling to land or money as if this life were everything. The result echoes the promise of Deuteronomy, “there will be no one in need among you”: “There was not a needy person among them.” Luke then introduces a man we will meet again and again, a Levite from Cyprus called Joseph, whom the apostles nicknamed Barnabas, “son of encouragement.” He sells a field and lays the money at the apostles' feet. Before Barnabas ever preaches a sermon, he gives. The Psalm crowns the risen Christ as king: “The LORD is king, he is robed in majesty.”

The Gospel continues the night conversation with Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel who came to Jesus in the dark. Jesus has told him that he must be born from above, of water and the Spirit, and Nicodemus cannot grasp it: “How can these things be?” Jesus answers with an image from the wind, which in Greek is the same word as Spirit: “The wind blows where it chooses, and you hear the sound of it, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit.” The newly baptized of Easter are exactly this: people born again, whose new life comes from a source the world cannot see. Then Jesus points to the cross. In the desert, when serpents were biting the people, Moses lifted a bronze serpent on a pole, and whoever looked at it lived. “So must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.” In John's Gospel “lifted up” means both the cross and the glory: the Son is raised on the wood and raised to the Father. Nicodemus does not understand tonight; but at the end of the Gospel he will come back in daylight, carrying a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes, to bury the One who was lifted up. The Spirit had been blowing in him all along.
outline: Ask: what would change in our parish if we really believed Christ is risen?
The Resurrection makes a family that shares.
The wind we cannot see but can hear.
Look at the cross and live; Nicodemus comes back.
“Whoever believes in him may have eternal life.”
live: Encourage one person by name today: a text, a visit, a word of thanks that lifts them up.
Spend three minutes before a crucifix and tell the Lord what is biting you; ask to be healed.
2027-04-06.prayer: Lord God, King robed in majesty, you raised your Son and lifted him up to your right hand. Pour out on us the Spirit who blows where he wills, and make us one heart and one soul, generous with what we have, encouraging to one another, and steady in our witness to the Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Son lifted up on the cross is made present on the altar, and at the elevation we look up at him as Israel looked at the serpent, and live. From the one Bread comes one heart and one soul.

quick: The first Christians were of one heart and soul and shared what they had, so that no one was in need.
Barnabas, the son of encouragement, sold his field and gave the money to the apostles.
Jesus told Nicodemus: as Moses lifted up the serpent, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, so that believers may have eternal life.
2027-04-06.action: Put aside something today, money, food or time, for a family in need in your parish.
2027-04-06.question: What do I hold on to as if Christ had not risen?

family.explain: After Jesus rose from the dead, his friends loved each other so much that they shared everything. Nobody was hungry and nobody was left out. A man called Barnabas even sold his field and gave the money to help the poor.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough food or a home.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share this week?” Choose one thing together and do it.

illus: In a parish in Alappuzha the youth group noticed that the same three families never came to the parish feast meal, because they could not pay the contribution. That Easter the young people quietly asked every household to put one handful of rice aside each day in a special tin. At the end of the Octave they had enough for the three families for two months. They called it the Barnabas tin. Nobody was told whose rice was whose.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, wind of God, blow through our hearts and make us one heart and one soul. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Everything they owned was held in common (Acts 4:32). What does my use of money say about my faith in the Resurrection?
Barnabas, which means son of encouragement (Acts 4:36). Who has been a Barnabas to me, and to whom can I be one?
So must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). What do I need to bring to the cross to be healed?
pm.resp: The Lord is king; he is robed in majesty.
interc: For the Church, that she may be one heart and soul, and that there may be no one in need among us.
For the poor of our parish and village, that they may find brothers and sisters in us.
For all who are discouraged, that God may send them a Barnabas.
For those seeking God in the dark like Nicodemus, that the Spirit may bring them to the light.
For our group, that we may look to the Crucified and Risen One and live.
pm.close: Father, your Son was lifted up so that all who believe may have life. Make us one in heart and generous in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Luke tells us that the first Christians were of one heart and soul, and no one said that anything he owned was his own (Acts 4:32). Why were they like this? Luke gives the reason in the very next sentence: with great power the apostles gave their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. When we really believe that Christ is risen, our grip on things loosens.

Then we meet Barnabas, son of encouragement. He sells a field and lays the money at the apostles' feet. Later he will be the one who welcomes the converted Saul when everyone else is afraid of him. A generous hand and an encouraging heart go together. Every parish needs its Barnabas.

In the Gospel Nicodemus is puzzled about being born again. Jesus says: the wind blows where it chooses; so it is with everyone born of the Spirit (John 3:8). We cannot see the Spirit, but we can see what he does: a selfish man begins to share, a frightened woman begins to speak, a family begins to pray again.

And Jesus points to the cross: as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). Look at him and live. Let us look at him today, at the altar where his sacrifice is made present, and ask him to make us one heart and soul, and to make each of us a Barnabas for someone this week. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, after Easter the friends of Jesus shared everything they had, so no one was hungry. A kind man called Barnabas gave away his field to help the poor, and everyone called him son of encouragement, because he always made people feel brave and happy. Can you be a Barnabas today? Say something kind to someone who is sad!

intro: Theme: “So must the Son of Man be lifted up.”
One heart and soul, born of the Spirit, and the cross that heals.

q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Now the whole group of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and no one claimed private ownership of any possessions, but everything they owned was held in common.
points.apply: Choose one possession you could share this week, a vehicle, a room, a skill, and offer it to someone in the parish.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
The wind blows where it chooses, and you hear the sound of it, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit.
points.apply: Thank God today for your baptism, and if you know the date, mark it on the calendar to celebrate each year.

q: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.
points.apply: At the elevation at your next Mass, look up at the Host and say silently: my Lord and my God, heal me.

concl: The Resurrection makes a community that shares, so that no one is in need.
The Spirit gives new birth, and the Son lifted up on the cross heals all who look to him.
2027-04-06.resolve: Be a Barnabas to one discouraged person each day this week.
